# Street Blackjack Radio: Technical Review Pack

For an independent technical review, and to check whether the radio can run on existing infrastructure. Everything here is self-contained and **separate from the live Street Blackjack system**.

**Repo snapshot:** `main` @ `68db724` (25 commits). **No secrets in the repo:** admin/API credentials only ever exist on the server in mode-600 files. **No audio in the repo:** test audio is generated by a script.

---

## 1. What it is (one minute)

```
            ┌──────────────────────── radio server (Docker) ────────────────────────┐
listeners ─►│ HTTPS reverse proxy ─┬─► AzuraCast  (Liquidsoap AutoDJ ×5 → Icecast)  │
  (game)    │  (Caddy, or yours)   │      /listen/<station>/radio.mp3, /hls/…, admin │
            │                      └─► Station Registry API (Node, read-only JSON)   │
            └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
external stations (e.g. OnTop FM) ◄── players connect directly; the registry only health-checks them
```

- **AzuraCast** (open source, stable channel) does broadcasting, scheduling, adverts and the admin UI. We configure it; we didn't fork it.
- **Registry API** (`/registry-api`): about 600 lines of Node, **no npm dependencies**. Merges AzuraCast's *public* now-playing data with external stations into one list for the game. Read-only, no auth, CORS allow-list.
- **Test player** (`/player`): plain HTML/JS PWA. Reference client, not the game UI.
- **Infra** (`/infra`): server hardening, AzuraCast install, reverse proxy, provisioning, test scripts.

## 3. Run the checks yourself

```bash
cd registry-api && npm test                     # 14 tests, Node 20+

# against any running AzuraCast (public endpoints only, no key needed):
node infra/scripts/check-continuous.mjs --base https://radio.<domain> --minutes 40
node infra/scripts/check-ads.mjs        --base https://radio.<domain> --minutes 30
# on the radio host itself:
node tools/load-test/load-test.mjs --base http://127.0.0.1:8080 --listeners 1000 --seconds 60
```

A full local environment (WSL2 + AzuraCast + registry + gateway) is described in `docs/stage2-local.md`.

## 4. Server requirements

| | Minimum (5 stations) | Recommended |
|---|---|---|
| CPU | 4 vCPU (x86_64 or ARM64) | 6–8 vCPU; **steady** CPU matters more than peak (each station encodes audio continuously, ~10% of a core per stream) |
| RAM | 4 GB | 8 GB+ |
| Disk | 40 GB + media | 200 GB NVMe. Media at 320 kbps ≈ 144 MB/hour; 50 h/station × 5 ≈ 36 GB, plus growth and backups |
| OS | Linux that runs Docker (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 tested) | Dedicated VM. Not OpenVZ/LXC (AzuraCast requirement). |
| Software | Docker + Docker Compose (AzuraCast's installer adds them) | |
| Network | 128 kbps per listener: **1,000 listeners ≈ 128 Mbit/s**; one listener 24/7 ≈ 43 GB/month | Unmetered or cheap egress (see cost model in stage1-findings §3) |
| Ports | 443 (and 80 for certificates) public. Optional SFTP 2022 for large uploads. | AzuraCast's own ports (8000–8999, 8080) **not** public |

## 5. Running it on your existing infrastructure

This works. The things to decide:

1. **Isolation from the game.** Put the radio on its **own VM/host** (or at least its own Docker host with CPU limits) and its own sub-domain. Liquidsoap needs steady CPU; if it's starved, audio stutters for every listener. And a radio problem must never touch the game, which was a requirement of the brief.
2. **Reverse proxy.** If you already run nginx/Traefik/Caddy with TLS, you don't need our Caddy. Route:
   - `radio.<domain>` → AzuraCast on its internal HTTP port (`AZURACAST_HTTP_PORT`, default 8080 in our install). **Disable response buffering** for `/listen/` and `/hls/` and allow very long-lived responses. nginx: `proxy_buffering off; proxy_read_timeout 24h;`.
   - `api.radio.<domain>` → registry container port 3000.
   - Send `X-Forwarded-For/Proto/Host` with the **bare host name, no port** (AzuraCast rejects `host:port`, see testing.md).
   - Block `/setup` publicly; optionally limit the admin UI to office/VPN IPs (our Caddyfile shows exactly which paths listeners need).
3. **Firewall.** Docker publishes ports past ufw/iptables rules. `bootstrap-server.sh` adds `DOCKER-USER` rules so AzuraCast's ports aren't reachable from the internet; replicate this on your hosts.
4. **Bandwidth cost.** Audio streaming is egress-heavy. On metered clouds (AWS/GCP/Azure/DO), 1,000 listeners 24/7 is ~215 TB/month. Check the price before choosing; this is why we recommended an unmetered host.
5. **Time sync.** Run NTP (chrony/systemd-timesyncd). Liquidsoap paces audio on the system clock. On our WSL2 test box the clock ran 3.5% slow and audio played at 0.97× speed (caught by the tests, fixed with chrony). Real servers with NTP are fine.
6. **Backups.** AzuraCast's scheduled backups (DB/settings, small) plus an off-site copy of media. See deployment.md §5.

## 6. Load test results (1,000 listeners)

**Setup:** AzuraCast stable, 5 stations each encoding MP3 128 kbps, on an 8-core / 12 GB WSL2 VM (Windows 10 PC). `tools/load-test/load-test.mjs` opened N simultaneous HTTP stream connections spread across the 5 stations, waited 10 s for Icecast's connect burst to pass, then measured each connection's byte rate for 50 s. Run **on the same machine**, so this measures the server software, not an internet link.

| Listeners | Got full rate (≥97% of 128 kbps) | Drops/errors | Per-listener rate (min / median / max) | Total out | AzuraCast CPU (of 8 cores) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 300 | **300 / 300** | 0 | 127.8 / 128.2 / 128.6 kbps | 38.5 Mbit/s | 0.3–1.05 cores |
| 1,000 | **1,000 / 1,000** | 0 | 127.4 / 128.0 / 128.6 kbps | 128.0 Mbit/s | 0.6–1.7 cores |

Raw output: `docs/results/stage4-load-300.log`, `docs/results/stage4-load-1000.log`.

**What it means:** one host comfortably serves 1,000+ listeners. In production the limits are the **network port and egress** (128 Mbit/s per 1,000) and **CPU steadiness** on shared vCPUs. For more, add AzuraRelay servers; the registry hands out relay URLs and the game doesn't change.

**What it doesn't cover:** real internet paths, real phones, or a different host's NIC. Re-run `load-test.mjs` on the target host (deployment.md §4).

## 7. Other test results (summary; details in testing.md)

- 40-min no-listener continuity: PASS. Mix changes gapless; the playlist loops.
- Adverts on 5 stations, 28 min: PASS. 10 breaks, all at mix boundaries.
- Scheduled show took over its slot and handed back at the next break: PASS.
- Restart/drop recovery: player reconnects in ~2 s; registry status stays correct.
- Security: listener-facing paths can't reach admin/setup/admin API; admin IP allow-list tested.
- **Not yet done:** real iPhone/Android device tests; production re-run; restore drill; OnTop FM real stream.

## 8. Known limitations / review points

- iOS doesn't allow web pages to set volume (Apple rule): use mute plus the hardware buttons.
- After a station *restart*, AzuraCast starts the next item rather than resuming mid-mix.
- Adverts only fall between files, hence the mix splitter (~30 min parts).
- Track-level licence reporting needs DJ tracklists (stations play whole mixes).
- The registry is a single instance (stateless; restart-safe with a snapshot on disk). Put it behind your existing health checks/restart policy.
